channel.title: Oddly
channel.description: Ideas on engineering autonomous agents, embedding trustworthiness, and learning from experience.

item.title: Verdicts require Epistemics
item.description: An autonomous agent investigates 5XX errors—and learns to separate what it observes, what it believes, and what it can safely do next.

item.title: Evidence requires Provenance
item.description: A precise number can tell the wrong story. Follow a claim back through the query, the cohort, and everything the summary left out.

item.title: State requires Ownership
item.description: The human paused the rollout. A late agent report says it is running. Which version of reality gets to win?

item.title: Autonomy requires a Dial
item.description: One agent can investigate freely, prepare a rollback, and still need permission to execute it. Authority belongs to the action.

item.title: Inputs require a Trust Boundary
item.description: A log line says the deployment is pre-approved. How does the system keep an observation from becoming an order?

item.title: Knowledge requires a Clock
item.description: The dashboard is accurate. It is also describing a world that has already changed. Truth needs a time boundary.

item.title: Delegation requires Ceilings
item.description: Every helper makes a reasonable request. Together, they overwhelm the system they came to investigate.

item.title: Failure requires a Ladder
item.description: When the agent loses its instruments, what should it give up first? Design the descent before the incident.

item.title: Learning requires Outcomes
item.description: The rollout looked healthy at thirty minutes. Four hours later, a queue filled. Who goes back and grades the earlier verdict?

item.title: Trustworthy Autonomy
item.description: Nine principles for systems that deserve the authority we give them. A field guide to evidence, boundaries, and learning from consequences.

item.title: What does “good” mean for an agent?
item.description: Quality begins with a shared understanding of what matters.

item.title: Engineering Autonomous Agents
item.description: Connecting intelligence, purpose, and action in systems we can depend on.

item.title: Skills aren’t policies
item.description: Knowing how to act and having the authority to act are different things.

item.title: Memory should accumulate judgment
item.description: Experience becomes useful when it improves the next decision.

item.title: Judgment Under Uncertainty
item.description: How should an autonomous system act when its understanding is incomplete?

item.title: Context engineering vs. harness engineering
item.description: Understanding the world and acting within it are connected engineering problems.

item.title: Why agent verifiers fail
item.description: Agreement is more useful when it comes from independent perspectives.
